findings.element: .b-rail, .b-todayRule, .b-tick and every --fore-NN ink step (b.css); no @media (forced-colors: active) exists in b.css, shell.css or master.html (grep count 0)
findings.problem: Driven in a Chromium context with forcedColors active at 1440x960 on state=owner-flight, the product loses the three marks it is built out of. .b-rail computes background rgba(255,255,255,0.16) against a forced Canvas ground: a 1x1530px element painting nothing, so the vertical line the whole design is named for is gone. .b-todayRule computes background rgb(255,255,255) at 344x1px on white, so today's rule is gone. Every .b-tick, including the lead tick that is the single indigo moment in the entire palette, forces to a Canvas fill with a CanvasText ring, so the one accent and the seven ordinary ticks become identical hollow circles. Because this design deliberately carries ALL status and hierarchy in ink density and fill rather than hue, forced-colors does not merely degrade it the way it degrades a colour-coded UI, it flattens the whole hierarchy to one weight of black on one white. Neither audit.mjs nor interaction-check.mjs ever instantiates a forced-colors context, so 499 assertions pass over a rendering mode in which the surface has no spine, no today and no next.
findings.fix: Add to b.css, after the interaction rules so it wins: @media (forced-colors: active) { .b-rail { forced-color-adjust: none; background: CanvasText; } .b-todayRule { forced-color-adjust: none; background: Highlight; height: 2px; } .b-tick { forced-color-adjust: none; background: Canvas; border: 1px solid CanvasText; } .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick, .b-item[data-anchor="true"] .b-tick { background: Highlight; border-color: Highlight; } .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-title { text-decoration: line-through; } } - three system colours only, so the palette lock is untouched (system colours are no more a fourth hue than the focus ring is), the spine and today survive, and the one accent moment keeps its distinction. Then add a forcedColors active pass over the state matrix to interaction-check.mjs asserting that .b-rail, .b-todayRule and the lead tick each still paint a fill that is neither transparent nor Canvas.

findings.element: .b-title with -webkit-line-clamp: 2 (b.css:213-216) plus the word-safe clamp() in render-core.js:200-215, on states phone / desk / day where a row deliberately holds no control
findings.problem: Driven at 390x844 with touch and mobile emulation on state=phone: setting one moment's name to "Drinks and canapes on the west lawn if the weather holds", 55 characters and entirely ordinary for a wedding, then calling __TLCORE.settle(), trims the visible row to "Drinks and canapes on the west lawn if the weather..." and parks the whole string in a title attribute and a .tl-vh twin. On a guest surface the row holds no control by design, there is no expand, and a tooltip cannot be summoned by a finger, so the guest on a phone (the flagship case, the one screen that judges the company) can never read the end of the sentence, while a screen-reader user gets all of it. Sighted touch users receive strictly less of the couple's own words than anyone else. The gate cannot see this because every title in fixture.js is short: querying [data-clamp][data-trimmed="true"] across phone, day, desk and publish at 390 returns zero elements, so the trim assertions currently pass vacuously on every guest state.
findings.fix: Two lines and a fixture edit. (1) In b.css scope the clamp to the owner's dense measure only: change the .b-title rule at 213 so -webkit-line-clamp: 2 applies under [data-state^="owner"] .b-title, and give guest rows -webkit-line-clamp: none with overflow: visible. render-b.js place() already re-places every row from measured geometry after settle(), so a three-line title only makes that day's row taller and nothing collides. (2) In fixture.js lengthen one moment name to a full sentence (for example "Drinks and canapes on the west lawn if the weather holds") so the trim, the fade and the collision assertions all run against a string that can actually trigger them.

findings.element: setTitle() in render-b.js:613-633, which writes data-full and textContent but never clears title / data-trimmed / the .tl-vh twin and never calls C.settle(); C.settle() is called from exactly one mutation path, the change handler at render-b.js:726
findings.problem: Driven at 390x844 on state=owner-editing: typing a long name into the editor field leaves the row at scrollHeight 103 against clientHeight 41, so the CSS safety net -webkit-line-clamp: 2 is doing the cutting, at the character, which is precisely the defect class lessons.md was paid for. At the same moment the row's title attribute still reads the OLD name ("Send the invitations") and data-trimmed is null with no full-string twin beside it. Only a window resize, the one thing that reaches settle(), repairs it: after a 1px viewport change the same node reads data-trimmed true and ends on a whole word. The invariant restorer is wired to mount, fonts.ready and resize, and to one mutation path out of several; every keystroke in between is a mid-word clip carrying a tooltip that describes a different moment.
findings.fix: In render-b.js setTitle(), immediately after title.setAttribute("data-full", shown) and title.textContent = shown, add title.removeAttribute("title"); C.settle(); - clamp() rebuilds from data-full, is idempotent by construction, and re-sets both the title attribute and the twin. Then assert it in interaction-check.mjs: after typing a 60-character title at 390 with no resize in between, .b-item[data-editing='true'] .b-title must have scrollHeight <= clientHeight + 1 and a title attribute equal to what was typed.

findings.element: --size-label through --size-countWide, shell.css:101-113 - thirteen steps, every one an absolute pixel, and now enforced at source in pixels
findings.problem: Setting document.documentElement.style.fontSize to 24px, which is exactly what a desktop reader who has raised their browser's default font size has done, leaves .b-title at 24px and .b-num at 148px. Nothing on the surface moves, because every step of the declared ladder is absolute. The audience here is a couple's families opening one screen, and some of them raised that setting years ago for a reason. Page zoom still works so this is not a total failure, but the one typographic preference a reader sets once and forgets is inert, and the audit gate grades the ramp's proportions rather than its units, so it will never say so.
findings.fix: Divide the thirteen values in shell.css:101-113 by 16 and express them in rem (11px becomes 0.6875rem, 148px becomes 9.25rem). Leave every other length in px so the space ladder, the measure geometry and the rail arithmetic are untouched. At a 16px root the rendered pixels are identical, so every audit.mjs ramp and leading assertion passes unchanged and the ladder stays exactly as declared.

findings.element: master.html:1, which opens <!doctype html> then <meta charset="utf-8"> with no <html> element at all; document.documentElement.lang evaluates to the empty string
findings.problem: There is no lang attribute anywhere in the artifact. A screen reader therefore speaks this plan in whatever voice the reader's machine defaults to, which on a non-English device turns "79 days away" and "Saturday 3 October 2026" into phonetic nonsense; browser translation and hyphenation have nothing to key off either. Every accessibility assertion in the gate is about names, roles, order and live regions, so nothing checks the single attribute that decides how all of those names are pronounced.
findings.fix: Emit <html lang="en-IE"> as the first element of master.html above the charset meta. build.mjs generates this file, so add it to the template there rather than to the generated output. Then assert it in interaction-check.mjs as "the document says what language it speaks": document.documentElement.getAttribute("lang") must be a non-empty BCP-47 tag in every state.

biggestWin: What holds my seat below 9.5 is that this master's correctness is proven at mount, at four widths, against one fixture whose strings are all too short to trim, and in one rendering mode - so the two regimes the product will actually meet, a moment name long enough to clamp and a machine running Windows forced-colors, are both unproven and both currently broken; call C.settle() from every mutation, give fixture.js one sentence-length moment name, and add a forced-colors block that redraws the rail, the today rule and the accent tick in system colours, and the gates start guarding the product instead of the fixture.
